sentences.text: Silvisaurus is a nodosaurid ankylosaur whose name combines Latin for woodland and Greek for lizard.
The skull measures 33 cm in length and 25 cm in width.
The lower jaw contains at least twenty-five teeth.
Each upper jaw bone holds between eight and nine teeth.
Large air passages in the head suggest the animal may have produced loud vocalizations for communication.
Teeth at the front of the jaw suggest Silvisaurus was a relatively primitive nodosaurid compared to later forms with beaks.
The species was discovered in the 1950s by Kansas rancher Warren W. Condray.
The dinosaur skeleton was recovered in July 1955 with the help of the discoverer.
The species was formally described and named by Theodore H. Eaton Jr. in 1960.
The genus name refers to the animal's likely habitat in a densely forested area.
The species name honors the rancher who discovered the fossil.
The holotype fossil was found in the Terra Cotta Clay Member of the Dakota Formation in Kansas.
The holotype consists of an incomplete skeleton including the skull, neck, back, tail, and leg bones.
Disarticulated armor plates and spikes were found alongside the main skeleton.
The fossil condition was poor due to exposure in a dry riverbed and damage from cattle.
Silvisaurus likely possessed bony spines on its shoulders and tail in addition to standard armor plates.
Silvisaurus is classified as a relatively primitive nodosaurid.
Research indicates Silvisaurus forms a basal group with Sauropelta and Pawpawsaurus, nested deep within the nodosaurid family tree.
Silvisaurus lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 113 to 105 million years ago, in what is now North America.
The time range for Silvisaurus is estimated from 106.3 to 100.5 million years ago.
It is debated whether Silvisaurus possessed bony spines on its shoulders and tail.
